lockFileMaintenance.description: Refresh lockfiles weekly so transitive deps don't drift even when no package.json range changes.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes bypass the weekly schedule, the minimum-release-age soak, and auto-merge once CI is green.

packageRules.description: Group all @nextcloud/* packages — peer deps couple them, so they should ship as one reviewable PR.

Group all Babel packages (single monorepo, lockstep releases). @nextcloud/babel-config is included because it peer-pins the @babel/core major — listed after the @nextcloud group so this groupName wins.
Group the ESLint + Stylelint linter stack so rule-config churn lands together.
Group the Vue ecosystem — Vue + vue-loader + Vue plugins move together with breaking-change implications.
Group webpack + its loaders/plugins — they share peer-dep constraints.
Don't touch nextcloud/ocp automatically — its dev-stableXX ref must follow info.xml max-version, which is a deliberate compat decision.

Don't bump the PHP floor — composer.json `php ^8.2` is a deliberate min-version statement tied to the Nextcloud versions we support, not something to drift with each new PHP release. Match on matchDepNames (not matchPackageNames): the composer manager gives the php constraint packageName `php/php-src`, so matchPackageNames:["php"] never fires; depName stays `php`.
Cap phpunit at <12: phpunit 12 needs PHP ^8.3 and phpunit 13 needs PHP ^8.4. Our floor is PHP 8.2. Revisit when raising the PHP minimum (which would also require bumping info.xml min-version).
Cap webpack-cli: @nextcloud/webpack-vue-config@7.0.2 peer-pins webpack-cli ^6. Remove this rule when upstream relaxes the peer.
Cap node-polyfill-webpack-plugin: @nextcloud/webpack-vue-config@7.0.2 peer-pins it to exact 4.0.0. Remove this rule when upstream relaxes the peer.

Cap postcss-html and stylelint-config-recommended-vue at <2: @nextcloud/stylelint-config@3.2.2 peer-pins stylelint-config-recommended-vue ^1.6.1, which in turn peer-pins postcss-html ^1. Both must move to v2 together, and only once upstream relaxes the peer. Remove this rule then.

Cap typescript at <7: TS 7 is the native (Go) port and no longer exposes the JS compiler API (require('typescript') only returns `version`). typescript-eslint (pulled in by @nextcloud/eslint-config) peer-pins typescript <6.1.0 and crashes on load with TS 7; ts-loader also needs the JS API. Remove this rule when typescript-eslint supports TS 7.
Don't auto-PR Vue or @nextcloud/{vue,dialogs} majors — they carry breaking changes that need coordinated source rewrites.
Automerge GitHub Actions minor + patch + digest updates — low risk, often.
Automerge devDependency patch updates — bug-fix-only churn that doesn't need eyes.
Never automerge runtime @nextcloud/* updates — their minors regularly ship breaking changes per Nextcloud's release policy.
Never automerge any major bump anywhere.
